# zoneblick

> zoneblick is a self-hosted DNS zone watchdog, written in Rust. It resolves each zone from the root, asks every authoritative nameserver directly, checks the answers for correctness and risk, and reports what changed. It is open source and runs on your own server; it is not a hosted service.

Status as of 2026-11-14: early development. These things work: `zoneblick check <zone>` checks a zone once: delegation, nameserver consistency, DNSSEC (beta), mail policy (SPF, DMARC, CAA, MTA-STS, MX) and takeover exposure (dangling aliases, and aliases, mail servers or SPF includes that point into unregistered domains); `zoneblick run <zone> --name <name>` also collects the records of listed names and stores each run in a SQLite file; `zoneblick diff <zone>` shows what changed between two stored runs, per nameserver. `zoneblick serve` runs as a daemon from a TOML config file: it checks zones on a schedule, sends alerts when something changes, and serves a JSON API and a web UI. There are 40 checks made on every run (some need a zone file, certificate logs or vantage points): delegation, nameserver consistency, DNSSEC, mail policy (SPF, DMARC, CAA, MTA-STS, TLS reporting, TLSA records for mail servers, DKIM keys, BIMI), takeover exposure (dangling aliases, unregistered domains, wildcard aliases, and aliases of unclaimed sites at 32 hosting services, matched by signature), certificates (with `--discover ct`: the newest logged certificate of a name about to expire, and certificates from an authority the CAA records do not allow), and drift from a zone file (`zoneblick run <zone> --expect <file>`). `zoneblick run <zone> --discover ct` finds more names in Certificate Transparency logs through crt.sh; `--discover axfr` by zone transfer; `--discover cloudflare|route53|gandi|hetzner|digitalocean` through the DNS host's API with a read-only credential (tested against recorded answers, not the live APIs). `zoneblick baseline pin <zone>` and `zoneblick diff <zone> --baseline` compare against a run pinned as correct; names whose addresses rotate are learned and not reported as changes; `zoneblick prune` and the daemon delete old runs (every run for 30 days, then one per day for a year). `zoneblick findings mute <zone> <id>` silences an accepted finding; `zoneblick export --format json|csv` writes the stored findings; `--sarif <file>` on `check` and `run` writes SARIF 2.1.0; `zoneblick zones add|remove` edits the zones in the database; `zoneblick digest` summarises a period. `zoneblick check <zone> --deep` (also `run --deep`, and `deep = "24h"` in the daemon's config) adds 21 deep checks (among them a mail server's certificate against its TLSA records, and signed proofs of absence): the DNSSEC chain of trust from the root's trust anchors down to the zone, signatures over every collected record set (RSA, ECDSA, Ed25519), denial-of-existence proofs, key rollover state, NSEC3 parameters, CDS/CDNSKEY consistency, algorithm completeness, EDNS compliance, open zone transfers, recursion on authoritative servers, query-name case, all nameservers in one network, reserved nameserver addresses, three SOA checks, and four registration checks read over RDAP (expiry, registry holds, transfer lock, nameservers on record). The daemon sends alerts by webhook, Slack, Discord, ntfy or email, can send a periodic digest, serves Prometheus metrics at /api/v1/metrics, and its web UI has a timeline of runs, a comparison of any two runs, muting and on-demand deep runs. `zoneblick plan <zone> --file <file>` checks a zone file before it is deployed and shows what deploying it would change. Several daemons can be compared as vantage points (`[[vantage]]` in the config). The daemon can listen on a unix socket (`bind = "unix:/path"`). HTTPS, SVCB, SRV and PTR records are collected. From v0.13.0, release files and the container image carry a build provenance attestation that `gh attestation verify` and the install script check. There is a GitHub Action (`uses: cschweda/zoneblick@v0.15.0`). Versions 0.12.0 and 0.13.0 each had a red team / blue team security audit (hostile DNS data, hostile HTTP, SMTP and API peers, hostile zone files, API attacks, supply chain); the README section "Security audits" records every audit, newest first, with what broke, what held and what is still open. The daemon can serve HTTPS itself (`tls_cert`, `tls_key`). From v0.14.0 the API and web UI always need a token; without `token_sha256` in the config the daemon makes one on first start in the file `api-token` in its data directory, and `zoneblick token --show <config>` prints it. The install script takes `--version`, `--prefix`, `--no-service` and `--require-attestation`. The README has a section of user stories ("Who it is for") and a section "Security" on how each part is protected. New in v0.15.0: eleven more deep checks (32 in all) that look past the zone's own nameservers: TKO-07 (a name delegated to nameservers that do not serve it), REG-05 (the registration of the domains the nameservers and mail servers are in), POL-11 (mail servers without STARTTLS or with an expired or wrong-name certificate), TLS-01 (the certificate a name really serves on port 443), NET-03 (route origin validation, RPKI, through RIPEstat), RES-01 and RES-02 (what the public resolvers of Cloudflare, Google and Quad9 say about the zone), BLK-01 (Spamhaus and SpamCop blocklists), POL-12 and POL-13 (weak SPF and DMARC records), LAL-01 (registered lookalike domains that take mail). The current release is v0.15.0, an early pre-release. Each release has ready-built binaries on the GitHub releases page (https://github.com/cschweda/zoneblick/releases) for Linux (x86_64 and ARM 64-bit, static), macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel, unsigned) and 64-bit Windows (unsigned). There are .deb and .rpm packages, a Homebrew formula (`brew tap cschweda/zoneblick https://github.com/cschweda/zoneblick`), and an install script for Linux and macOS (`curl -fsSL https://zoneblick.com/install.sh | sh`) and a container image at ghcr.io/cschweda/zoneblick. It can also be built from source with a stable Rust toolchain (1.88 or later): `cargo install --git https://github.com/cschweda/zoneblick`. The name is always written in lowercase.

Key facts:

- Author: Christopher Schweda
- Language: Rust
- License: MIT or Apache-2.0, at your option
- Source code: https://github.com/cschweda/zoneblick
- It queries authoritative nameservers itself, over UDP and TCP, IPv4 and IPv6. It never trusts a recursive resolver's cache.
- It is meant for zones you control. It is not an offensive or scanning tool.

## Site

- [Home](https://zoneblick.com/): what DNS drift is, what zoneblick checks, how a run works, and how it differs from existing tools
- [Demo](https://zoneblick.com/demo.html): the planned web interface, shown with sample data only

## Documentation

- [README](https://github.com/cschweda/zoneblick/blob/main/README.md): how to try the `check` command, exit codes, and the JSON output format
- [Design document](https://github.com/cschweda/zoneblick/blob/main/DESIGN.md): goals, architecture, the full check catalog, data model and build phases
- [Decisions](https://github.com/cschweda/zoneblick/blob/main/DECISIONS.md): choices made during implementation, one line each

## Optional

- [Zonemaster](https://zonemaster.net): deep one-shot delegation and DNSSEC analysis; zoneblick does not aim for parity
- [DNSViz](https://dnsviz.net): DNSSEC chain visualisation
